div.div: عَرْتُنٌ , (S, K, * [in the K it is not clear whether this be thus or عَرَتُنٌ,]) and عَرْتَنٌ, (S, K,) and عَرَتَنٌ, [thus accord. to copies of the K,] with تَحْرِيك, (K, TA,) and with kesr to the ت, (TA, [which may mean that it is عَرَتَنٌ and عَرَتِنٌ or only the latter, but what is meant in the K is evidently عَرَتَنٌ,]) originally ↓ عَرَنْتُنٌ , like قَرَنْفُلٌ, (Kh, S, K,) and ↓ عَرَنْتَنٌ , or both and ↓ عَرَنْتِنٌ , as also ↓ عَرَتُونٌ , (K,) A species of plant, (S,) or tree, (K,) rough, resembling the عَوْسَج [or boxthorn], except that it is bigger, full and luxuriant in the branch, and not having tall stems, (TA, [see also عِرْنَةٌ, of which the same is said,]) with which, (S, K, TA,) it being [first] cooked, (TA,) one tans, (S, K, TA,) and the hide tanned therewith becomes red. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
